recipes.name: Classic Pecan Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 cup Karo Light or Dark Corn Syrup
1 (9 inch) unbaked deep dish pie crust

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix corn syrup, sugar, eggs, butter, and vanilla extract together in a large bowl with a spoon; stir in pecans.
Bake in the preheated oven until center reaches 200 degrees F (95 degrees C), and it springs back when lightly touched, 60 to 70 minutes. If crust becomes too brown, cover edges with foil.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Pecan Pie
raw_recipe.description: This pecan pie recipe combines eggs, corn syrup, vanilla, and pecans in a pie crust. Bake until golden brown for a classic Thanksgiving dessert.

review.reviewBody: Ok, I made my first pecan pie ever about 6 weeks ago at Thanksgiving. I loved it...but being my first time, I felt I should try out other recipes. Comparatively, this recipe is nearly identical to my first one, with just a few variations to the measurements and also using entirely light Karo (mine used half dark) and also using gran sugar instead of brown. Flavor and texturally speaking it was about the same. BUT!!!!! The simplest step ever was missing from this recipe -- IF YOU WANT TO MAKE THIS PIE...*please*, I implore you, toast the pecans first!! Nothing to it, put them all into a non-stick skillet over med heat...about 6 minutes total, and tossing if necessary to prevent burning. This is such a critical, flavor-enhancing step and it makes all the difference in the world. I promise. Happy cooking....

Here's a hint to keep the edges of the pie crust from over-browning. Spray the underside of a crust protector ring with non-stick spray and place it on the unbaked pie before putting the pie in the oven. Do not remove the ring until the pie is finished baking. The crust will still brown nicely while covered. I do this for all of my quiches and two crust pies. I make my own rings out of heavy duty foil and they work like a charm.

My mom showed me this recipe years ago. It is the only one I have ever used, though I often add more pecans. Covering the crust edge when baking is a must so it doesn't get too browned. The filling can be sticky when baking. I used to cover the crust edge with tinfoil, until I found a flexible silicone crust ring. One year, after starting to make the pie, I discovered I was out of vanilla so I used almond extract instead. That was the best pie ever! Now, I always skip the vanilla and use almond extract.

This was a very easy and delicious recipe. I followed the suggestion to roast the pecans for about 5 min in a skillet first and I added about 2 tbsp molasses with the Karo syrup to make the 1 cup the recipe calls for and it added a rich flavor. I will definitely use this recipe in the future.

easy to make and good to eat. good recipe for first timers. I used finely chopped pecans because they are easier for my father-in-law to eat, for a prettier pie definitely go with pecan halfs. rather than mixing them in try arranging them in bottom of crust and pour filling over them. they will rise to the top.
I made it for Thanksgiving and people loved it! I did substitute 1/3 of the corn syrup with maple syrup. I also toasted the pecans which makes a big difference.

I messed my other review up so I will try this again... made this yesterday. My first time attempting pecan pie. It was awesome. I did do a few adjustments, not on the original recipe but a few enhancements I guess. I toasted the pecans which I think was a great thing for the flavor. I whipped the eggs until foamy which I think helped give it a lighter texture. I also made a thick dark chocolate ganache and spread that on the bottom of the pie shell and then added the pecan pie filling. The dark chocolate I think really enhanced the flavors of this pie, and made the super sweetness of it come together. My husband said I can no longer make his favorite cake for his birthday, he only wants this pie.

Pecan pie is one if my favorites and this pie was really good. My family really liked it. The only change I made was using half brown sugar and half white. My only advice would be to cover the edge of the crust with foil...my crust was darker then the pie filling. :(
I made 2 slight changes. I added 1/4 cup of brown sugar and 3/4 cup of white sugar. I also added a dash of cinnamon.

I made this 3 times this year, and here is what I learned. You can increase the heat to 400 for the first 15 minutes and that helps it set up. Also adding a tablespoon of flour helps with that too. I left the pecans whole for two of the pies and chopped them for the third. My family liked the whole pecan ones better. The difference was the whole ones floated to the top and got kind of roasted there. They liked that flavor. The chopped ones stayed more suspended in the mixture, but the pie was easier to cut and eat. I thought the flavor was still very nice on the chopped pecan one. I also reduced the sugar by a 1/4 cup and it was plenty sweet.
I added 1 teaspoon of molasses, as I used Karo lite. Perfect!
Super easy recipe! I wish I could include a picture. It's so beautiful.

The flavor of this pie is lovely; so much better and 'natural' than commercial pecan pies. I lightly toasted the pecans before adding them to the filling. However, I waited until the filling was 200 degrees on the food thermometer and it was over-cooked around the edges. Next time, I will take it out when it is set in the middle as I have done in the past.
I followed directions exactly and the filling was too runny. No idea why!!
I used bourbon instead of vanilla, wasn't impressed with the flavor. Would've been better with vanilla. Next time.
No changes made. It came out perfect. Easiest pecan pie recipe
Sweet but not too sweet.
I added an extra egg, dry roasted the nuts for about 3 minutes, and used half caro and half maple syrup. I also used a graham cracker crust. Simply delish!

So easy, so good. Used the molasses idea, yeah try it. I usually double the recipe except for pecans. In second pie use raisins. Then you get a pecan pie and a raisin pie… just like a 9in butter tart 😀😉
No simple and delicious
